newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia unlikely to reach jobs target-Opposition.
newsitem.headline: Australia unlikely to reach jobs target-Opposition.

text.p: Australia's Labor opposition said on Thursday the May unemployment data meant the government was unlikely to reach its 1996/97 employment growth forecast.

"To meet the government's revised budget forecasts for average employment growth of 1.25 percent for 1996/97 there would now need to be 185,000 new jobs created next month," opposition labour spokesman Martin Ferguson said in a statement.

The seasonally adjusted estimate of the number of employed persons fell 40,300 in May to 8.380 million. The jobless rate rose to 8.8 percent from 8.7 percent in April, compared with a seasonally adjusted 8.5 percent a year earlier.

Ferguson also said the Liberal-National government forecast was unlikely to meet its employment growth forecast of 2.0 percent in the year to June 30, 1998. "The likely outcome will be just half that forecast - barely one percent," he said.
The fall in the participation rate to 63.2 percent in May from 63.5 percent in April added to the government's woes, he said.
The jobless rate has remained stubbornly high at around 8.5 percent since the conservative government entered office in March 1996.
